blocks.content: Suppose we let $f(\mathbf{x})$ be a scalar (single-dimension) function of a column vector, $\mathbf{x} = (x_1, \cdots, x_n)^T$, of $n$ variables. The gradient (or gradient vector) of $f$ with respect to $\mathbf{x}$ is obtained by taking partial derivatives of the function with respect to each variable. In matrix notation, the gradient operator is denoted by $$ \nabla\mathbf{x}[f]=\frac{\partial f}{\partial\mathbf{x}}=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_{1}}\\ \vdots\\ \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_{n}}\end{pmatrix} $$
The gradient at a point, $ x_{o} $, corresponds to a vector indicating the direction of local steepest ascent of the function at that point (the multivariate slope of $ f $ at $ x_{o} $).
